title: OpenAI v1 chat: strict-mode param + stop-weighting + structured-stream framing
author: Priya Singh
description: Context: Several customers asked for a more deterministic OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility mode that preserves the intent of "stop" semantics and makes logprob outputs easier to reconcile with framed streaming responses. Motivation: existing heuristics allowed ambiguous stop truncation when mixed with function/tool calls and streaming fragments, and logprob placement varied across framing changes. This PR introduces a conservative "strict_mode" param on the v1 adapter, a stop-weighting adjustment that biases token-level stop scoring toward earlier stop matches, and a compact structured framing envelope for streamed json fragments so downstream adapters can consistently attach logprobs and toolcall metadata. Changes (high level): 1) API: add optional query param/body field "strict_mode" (boolean) to /v1/chat.completions adapter; when enabled we enforce earlier stop precedence and stricter role-message ordering checks. 2) Stop handling: implement stop-weighting augmentation (configurable coefficient exposed only via adapter) that adjusts the stop detection score to prefer shorter matches and earlier token boundaries; documented nuance with overlapping multi-token stops. 3) Streaming: introduce a compact framed-json envelope for delta chunks that has explicit "final_chunk" and "logprob_meta" slots so function/tool call boundaries are unambiguous across chunk boundaries. 4) Logprobs: move best-effort logprob emission to the final envelope for partial messages but keep token-level provisional logprobs on intermediate frames for lower-latency UIs. 5) Tests: end-to-end suite that exercises partial tool calls crossing stream fragments and mixed stop lists. 6) Docs: API compatibility section describing strict_mode semantics and recommended client migration steps. Checklist: - [x] design doc (ENG-5271) - [x] unit tests for stop heuristics - [x] e2e tests for streaming toolcall boundaries - [x] docs update in redwood-docs - [x] performance sanity check on runtime path (no measurable 99th p99 regression) Backwards-compat: default behavior unchanged; strict_mode is opt-in. Risks and mitigations: stop-weighting may change borderline completions that previously returned an extra token; we added a safety toggle and a short rollout (canary) on dedicated clusters before platform-wide enablement. Related: ENG-5320 (tool-call fragmentation incident followup), ENG-5199 (openai-compat parity work).

review_thread: Ellen Park: Please explain the rationale for preferring earlier stop matches — can this cause legitimate truncations if a model prefers a longer stop sequence later?

Priya Singh: Short answer: strict_mode trades some recall for deterministic truncation. Longer stop matches can still be returned when not ambiguous, but strict_mode ensures consistency for downstream tooling that relies on exact cut points. Added more notes in docs.

Marcus Li: The streaming envelope looks good; add a small version header to allow future migration. Also please ensure the envelope is backwards compatible with older client parsers (we added a compatibility shim).
Priya Singh: Added a 1-byte "v" version marker to framed envelope, and streamer falls back to legacy framing when version absent. Test added.
Noah Kaplan: CI shows a flaky test in streamer_integration_test.go — observed timeout on sandbox env. Can we increase wait time or improve readiness?
Priya Singh: Increased the watcher timeout and replaced a sleep-based probe with an event-driven readiness check; re-ran CI.
release_notes: Opt-in 'strict_mode' for /v1/chat.completions to enforce deterministic stop precedence; stop-weighting heuristic to favor earlier stop matches; compact framed-json streaming envelope to make toolcall/logprob attachment unambiguous across chunks. Default behavior unchanged.
